text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- Egypt will cross the threshold of the next century with a complete vision for the future and a strong will to face the challenges. President Mubarak delivers a speech on the occasion on Police Day: We are waging a struggle to complete grand historical and national projects.
- The president oversees the internal and external security situation at the police academy.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri tells an economic forum: new legislation will provide opportunities for the private sector.
- Ganzouri to hold a meeting on privatisation today.
- Mubarak sends a letter to Saudi King Fahd. Egypt does not accept the partition of Sudan and the Sudanese people must reach an accord to save their country.
- A huge terrorist attempt aborted in Minya and three terrorists killed.
- Reports about the death of the head of Kurmuk town in Sudan.
AL-AKHBAR
- Mubarak at Police Day festivities: We are waging a full-scale attack to change life in Egypt.
- The president will attend Egypt's international celebration marking the Night of Quranic Revelation.
- The foreign minister: We refuse the partition of Sudan under any circumstances.
- Egypt, Senegal football squads in 0-0 tie.
- Egypt's Mufti, the highest-ranking religious official says the beliefs of the devil worshippers contradict all religions.
AL-GOMHURIA

- Mubarak says: Egypt is at a new launching stage and needs the efforts of every Egyptian. Security is an attraction to foreign and local investment. Our duty is to work day and night without stopping or even resting.
- Ganzouri says 1997 will witness new legislature to encourage investment.

- In the exciting testimonies of the devil worshippers: we stole human skulls from the graves for our wild parties. Black lipstick to attract fashion-concious females and the inspiration came from the United States and Israel.
$1 = 3.4 Egyptian pounds
